item.title: Summer Tree ID — Fri Aug 7, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Summer Tree ID With Lauren Lampley Friday, August 7 | 10am – 1pm BRN – Core | BREG – Elective Register Here!
Join this class as we discuss how to use different characteristics and field guides to identify common trees of Western North Carolina. By June, most trees will be fully leafed-out for the year which will make Identification much easier in most cases. We will talk about using multiple clues to identify trees as well as some of the natural history of the trees we find on property. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. item.title: Pisgah Ridge & Graveyard Ridge — Mon Aug 10, 8:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **THE HIKE:** Start at Graveyard Field parking lot. Cross the BRP and take a social trail south, up to Pisgah Ridge. At the ridge line, turn right and proceed along the ridge line until reaching Black Balsam Road (FSR 816). Take a social trail that parallels Black Balsam Rd to Art Loeb/MST. Climb to where that trail crosses Black Balsam Rd. and then continue on the MST. We'll take a break along this section. Hike down to Black Balsam Junction and take the Graveyard Ridge Trail (not MST) and Graveyard Ridge Trail Connector trail back to the parking lot.
**TRAIL CONDITIONS:** Some sections of the social trails are overgrown. LONG TROUSERS ARE REQUIRED. Also, bring rain gear for later in the day. Distance is about 7 miles, and pace will be about 2 mph. I expect spending 4 hrs on the trail. Elevation is easily 1,000+ feet. This is not an easy hike. Gardening with an Ecological Mindset with Nina Shippen Two sessions: Wednesday, August 12 | 9:30 am – 12 pm and Wednesday, August 19 | 9:30 am – 12 pm BREG – Core (Qualifies for EcoGardening core class) Register Here!
Gardening with an Ecologic Mindset introduces theories, research, and models from ecology that a gardener can use to create robust, resilient, and beautiful landscapes that can support the diverse plant, insect, and animal communities found in a healthy ecosystem. The course is a springboard from which students can later explore gardening topics in more depth, such as gardening on slopes, managing stormwater, creating hedgerows, invasive plants, and grappling with native vs. exotic controversies. Nina Shippen practices residential landscape and garden design through her company Hidden Road Landscape Design, which focuses on coupling the principles of healing gardens with sound ecologic practices to create satisfying gardens for her clients. item.title: Geology of the Blue Ridge I — Thu Aug 13, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Geology of the Blue Ridge I With Anton DuMars Thursday, August 13 | 12 – 4pm BRN – Core Register Here!
This is the first class of a two-part Geology course that explores the geologic history of the Southern Appalachian Mountains with lecture presentations, discussions and self-guided explorations in the field. The course begins with a discussion of the earth’s interior and plate tectonics, progresses to a model for the formation of the southern Appalachians and then describes the surficial processes that generate the current mountain topography. Discussion will also include an overview of geologic processes that affect these mountains today: earthquakes, mass movements and floods. Anton DuMars, a resident of Black Mountain, NC, is an adjunct professor at the College of Charleston. His geological interests include fluvial, deltaic, and coastal processes. item.title: Graybeard Falls -- 6 mi, 1,200 ft. gain — Fri Aug 14, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **[Sign-up opens Sunday, Aug. 9th at 8 PM]**
The Mt. Graybeard Trail is a favorite of many, myself included. We’ll do an out-and-back, around 3.1 miles up, then the same coming back. There's a clearing by Graybeard Falls where we'll take a little break before heading down.
This is not an easy hike! Because of the long uphill segment and lots of heads-down walking over roots & rocks, I’m giving this a solid 5.0 difficulty level on a 10-point scale. We'll move at a fairly good pace, averaging around 2.3 mph. If you're a first-timer and unsure if you're good with 1,000'+ elevation gains, it's best not to attend this one and risk holding back the group.
If you ever use hiking poles, they'd be useful here. Prepare for a trio of stream crossings with some potential rock-hopping depending on water levels. The trail can be muddy in parts, too. Yes, this hike can be a bit sloppy, but it's worth it!
Wear good hiking shoes, bring some water, and a little snack if so

item.title: Bonsai Exhibit Talk and Tour with Arthur Joura — Tue Aug 18, 5:30 PM
item.description:
Bonsai Exhibit Talk and Tour with Arthur Joura Tuesday, August 18 | 5:30 – 7pm Register Here!
Join Bonsai Curator Arthur Joura on this entertaining and informative after-hours tour of the garden at its peak in summer, a fitting showcase for the specimens and the miniature landscapes. As Joura says, “The two things are one: The garden is designed to elevate the experience of bonsai, and the bonsai never look better than when they’re on display in the garden.” This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Arthur Joura has been the bonsai curator at the Arboretum since 1992 and oversaw the design and development of the Arboretum’s Bonsai Exhibition Garden. Joura augmented early training in fine art and studied bonsai with some of the leading bonsai authorities in the United States and in Japan. His greatest teachers are trees, however. item.title: Summer Wildflowers of the NC Arboretum — Sat Aug 22, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Summer Wildflowers of the NC Arboretum with Lauren Lampley Friday, August 22 | 10 – 1pm BRN – Core | BREG – Core Register Here!
Interested in learning how to identify wildflowers? Join Lauren on this walk around the Arboretum property where we will go over different ways of identifying plants and different families of flowers. Some flowers are very difficult to identify to species and some are relatively easy so we will talk about how to get as close as possible with tools we can easily carry into the field. We will be using Newcomb’s guide to key out some of the less common flowers but will focus on learning how to look closely at flowers to identify them. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. item.title: An introduction to the Amphibians of the Southern Appalachians — Sat Aug 22, 12:00 PM
item.description:
An Introduction to the Amphibians of the Southern Appalachians with Carlton Burke Saturday, August 22 | 12 – 4pm BRN – Core Register Here!
The forested slopes, mountain streams and rivers, and valleys and floodplains of our southern mountains provide unique habitats for a variety of cold-blooded amphibian life. In this class we’ll focus on many of the various species found here, their specialized habitats and life cycles, and threats to their existence. Class participants will also have a chance to meet in the classroom, a few live amphibian residents of our mountain region. Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. He also was on the staff of the western North Carolina Nature Center in Asheville for over 25 years as the Curator of Exhibits. item.title: Tomato Jam 2026 — Sun Aug 23, 12:30 PM
item.description: Welcome to The Tomato Jam! Join us at The Mule in Asheville, North Carolina for a celebration of Western North Carolina’s favorite summer crop—the tomato. The Tomato Jam brings together farmers, growers, chefs, makers, musicians, gardeners, and food lovers for a day of local food, live music, community, and Appalachian culture. From heirloom tomatoes and farm-fresh produce to tomato-inspired dishes, handcrafted goods, and great music, The Tomato Jam celebrates everything that makes Western North Carolina special. We’re looking for tomato growers, chefs, restaurants, makers, artisans, nonprofits, and businesses that share a passion for local food, agriculture, and community. Whether you grow them, cook them, preserve them, paint them, or simply love them, we’d love to have you join us. Admission is FREE. Vendor participation is FREE. Vendors keep 100% of their sales. We proudly support ASAP Connections and encourage vendors and attendees to learn more about their mission support
